app.description: A free point-of-care ultrasound logbook. Log scans and clips, track RCEM, FAMUS, FUSIC, EUSEM, ACEM, CPoCUS and ACEP targets, get signed off and assessed, and export portfolio-ready PDFs with QR-verified summaries.
app.title: Your logbook. In your pocket.
app.lede: Log a scan in seconds from a photo you take or an image you upload. Your supervisor signs it off on the spot or from a secure link, and anyone checking your portfolio confirms it is genuine by scanning a QR code. Free, and your photos never leave your phone.
app.ios: On iPhone: tap Share in Safari, then Add to Home Screen. Wavelength then opens full screen like any app.
app.featTitle: Everything your training asks for, in one place.
app.f1Text: Pick the scan type, tick the findings and add images or short clips. The built-in editor crops, rotates and blacks out identifiers before anything is saved.
app.f2Text: Progress bars for each module show scans, supervised scans, required findings and assessments, and the app tells you what to focus on next.
app.f3Text: Your supervisor signs on your phone, from a link on their own phone or from their dashboard, and rates image quality and diagnostic accuracy.
app.f4Text: DOPS, formative and summative assessments, scored across six domains and signed by the assessor, each with its own verification code.
app.f5Text: Every sign-off, assessment and summary has a code and QR code. Scanning it shows the record as it was signed, so an edited file does not match.
app.f6Text: Export PDF, Excel or CSV with a verified summary, and follow the steps for your e-portfolio, college or appraisal.
app.privText: Photos and clips stay on your phone and in backup files you save to your own cloud. Only the written record syncs to your account, and it must never contain patient identifiers. Images you share in a sign-off link are encrypted on your phone first, so Wavelength stores files it cannot open, and deletes them once your supervisor signs.
app.langText: The app works in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Polish, Arabic, Russian and Chinese. Choose your language on the first screen or in Me at any time. Exports, certificates and verification records stay in English so any reviewer reads them the same way.
app.a1: Yes. The logbook, progress tracking, sign-off, assessments, exports and backups are free.
app.q2: Does Wavelength see my scan photos?
app.a2: No. Photos stay on your phone and in backups you save yourself. Images you include in a sign-off link are encrypted on your phone, and Wavelength cannot open them.
app.a3: Yes, a free Wavelength account. Every scan, sign-off and verified summary then belongs to a named clinician, which makes it trustworthy evidence.
app.q4: Will my college or accrediting body accept it?
app.a4: The logbook records what the published curricula ask for, and verified summaries let reviewers check your evidence online. Your supervisor and the accrediting body decide what they accept, so check with them.
app.q5: Is it in the App Store and Google Play?
app.a5: Store versions are on the way. Until then you install it from this website in two taps, and it works like any app, including offline.
app.q6: Can my supervisor use it in another language?
app.a6: Yes. Sign-off links and assessment pages open in the supervisor's browser language when it is one of the nine.

about.description: Wavelength is a point-of-care ultrasound education provider for emergency and acute clinicians, founded by an emergency medicine consultant in the UK.
about.title: On the same wavelength.
about.lede: Good teaching happens when teacher and learner tune in to each other. Good scanning happens when you tune the image until the answer is clear.
about.p1: Wavelength started from a simple observation in the emergency department. Clinicians leave many ultrasound courses with a certificate but little confidence, because they spent the day watching rather than scanning.
about.p2: We build each course the other way round: short, focused teaching, live demonstration, then supervised time on the probe in groups of four or five.
about.p3: Learning does not stop when the course ends. Wavelength Pearls teach one technique at a time, Wavelength Academy builds them into certified modules, and the Wavelength app keeps your logbook, sign-offs and assessments in one place, wherever you train.
about.firas: Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Ultrasound Lead at Darent Valley Hospital, Kent. Scanning since 2008 and teaching ultrasound since 2010. FAMUS instructor and supervisor, member of the EUSEM Ultrasound Committee and the Emergency Ultrasound Curriculum Task Force, European Board examiner, ALS and ATLS instructor.
about.zahra: Emergency medicine specialist and experienced ultrasonographer. She runs Wavelength day to day, from course planning to delegate support.
about.companyText: Wavelength is the trading name of Auda Medical Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales. Courses take place in the UK and are taught in English.
